sections.h2: Where is Huntley, Illinois, and why does it sit in two counties?
sections.html:
Huntley is a village in the northwest Chicago area that straddles McHenry County and Kane County. It lies along Interstate 90, covers about 14.29 square miles of land, and uses ZIP code 60142. Three townships divide it: Grafton, Rutland and Hampshire.

The village's own FAQ gives the township split. Land north of Kreutzer Road is in Grafton Township, and land south of Kreutzer Road is in Rutland Township, except the northwest end of Sun City, which is in Hampshire Township. The county and township matter to a seller because they decide which office handles your tax bill and your deed.

Huntley was founded in 1851 and incorporated in 1872, and it is named for Thomas Stillwell Huntley. Its census count was 5,730 in 2000, 24,291 in 2010 and 27,740 in 2020, one of the sharpest growth curves in the region.

sections.h2: What do the Census numbers say about Huntley homeowners?
sections.html:
The Census Bureau estimated 29,132 residents on July 1, 2025, up 5.0 percent from the April 2020 base. For 2020 to 2024 it reports an owner-occupied rate of 88.9 percent, a median value of owner-occupied homes of $334,300, and 12,213 households averaging 2.29 people. Median household income is $88,536, and the mean commute is 29.5 minutes.

The age profile is the most unusual part. QuickFacts lists 34.1 percent of residents as 65 or older and only 3.2 percent under 5. The 2020 census put the median age at 48.2.

  • A high share of older residents often means estate sales, downsizing and moves to be near family.
  • With 88.9 percent of homes owner-occupied, most sales here are owner-to-owner rather than investor deals.
  • Sun City, the age-restricted community reached by Del Webb Boulevard, is its own submarket and has its own garbage arrangement according to the village.

sections.h2: What drives the local economy and the roads around Huntley?
sections.html:
Growth in new businesses and distribution warehouses, especially along Illinois Route 47, has shaped the last decade. A small downtown keeps restaurants and shops. Route 47 is the main north-south road and runs nearly seven miles through the village. It was widened from two to five lanes in 2011, carries over 20,000 vehicles a day, and meets I-90 at a full interchange that was finished in November 2013.

Algonquin Road, a four-lane divided highway, runs east toward Algonquin and Lake in the Hills, and Main Street connects west toward Marengo and Harmony Road. Huntley-Dundee Road leads east to the Carpentersville and Dundee area. The Union Pacific Belvidere Subdivision passes through, and many local industries sit near the tracks.

Huntley once planned a stop on a proposed Metra intercity line from Rockford to Chicago, but it withdrew over concerns about its downtown. A listing can point to the I-90 and Route 47 access as a practical selling point.

sections.h2: Which schools and services come with a Huntley address?
sections.html:
Huntley Community School District 158 serves the village. Huntley High School is on Harmony Road, and the middle schools are Marlowe in Lake in the Hills and Heineman in Algonquin. Elementary schools include Leggee in Huntley, Martin and Chesak in Lake in the Hills, and Conley and Mackeben in Algonquin.

  • The Huntley Fire Protection District covers about 55 square miles and serves all village residents.
  • The Huntley Area Public Library is on Ruth Road. The Hampshire Township part of the village is served by the Ella Johnson Memorial Public Library.
  • The Huntley Park District runs the recreation center on Mill Street.
  • Residential garbage goes through a single village-wide hauler with Monday pickup, except apartments and Sun City.
  • Overnight parking on village streets is prohibited from 2 a.m. to 6 a.m., which matters when buyers or movers visit.

Huntley is a home rule municipality with an elected village president and a six-member board of trustees.

sections.h2: Does Huntley charge a transfer stamp, and what else applies at closing?
sections.html:
No. The village's FAQ says Huntley does not require a real estate transfer stamp, and it also says the village does not require village stickers.

State law still applies. Illinois also taxes the transfer of title itself under 35 ILCS 200/31-10, and a mortgage the buyer takes over can be left out of the taxable value if the deed says so. Ask the title company which county charges apply to a McHenry County parcel and which to a Kane County parcel.

Most home improvements in the village need a permit, and Development Services at 847-515-5252 can confirm whether a past project was permitted. If you finished a basement, deck or similar work, find the permit paperwork before you list.

sections.html:

sections.h2: What village rules does a buyer inherit with a Huntley house?
sections.html:
Buyers often ask about local rules before they make an offer, and the village FAQ answers several of them.

  • Watering follows a four-tier color-coded conservation program (red, yellow, orange and green), with signs posted around the village.
  • The village applies the McHenry County Open Burning Ordinance to all property inside its limits, and because lots are small, leaf burning is essentially illegal for most homeowners.
  • There is no village pet license, but McHenry and Kane counties both require rabies tags for dogs.
  • A garage sale needs no permit, though signs may go only on private property.
  • Recreational vehicle parking and storage fall under Zoning Code Section 156.106.
  • Yard waste is collected from April 1 to November 30, and the village runs a branch pick-up program twice a year.

Handing a buyer this short list in advance saves questions during negotiations, and it shows the house has been looked after.

sections.h2: How can you sell a Huntley house quickly?
sections.html:
Three routes are open, and the right one depends on how much work the house needs and how soon you must close.

  • Hire an agent and list. This tends to reach the most buyers, and Huntley's owner-heavy market suits it when the house is in good shape.
  • Sell it yourself. You keep the whole process in your hands, including the contract and the disclosures.
  • Take a cash offer. It can work for an inherited house, a rental, or a place that needs repairs you do not want to fund, and the closing date can be set around your plans.

Before choosing, confirm the county for the parcel, collect any permit records, and ask the water billing office about a final reading. With no village stamp to buy, Huntley sales can move on a short schedule once the contract is signed.

faqs.q: What is the population of Huntley, IL?
faqs.a: The Census Bureau estimated 29,132 residents on July 1, 2025. The 2020 census counted 27,740.

faqs.q: Does Huntley require a real estate transfer stamp?
faqs.a: No. The Village of Huntley's FAQ states that it does not require a real estate transfer stamp or village stickers. Illinois state transfer tax still applies.
McHenry County and Kane County. Land north of Kreutzer Road is in Grafton Township, and most land south of it is in Rutland Township.
Huntley Community School District 158 serves the village, with Huntley High School on Harmony Road.

faqs.q: Who do I call about property taxes on a Huntley house?
faqs.a: Call the McHenry County Assessor's Office at 815-334-4290 or Kane County at 630-232-5950, depending on where the parcel lies. The township numbers are in the table above.
